title: Mean confused with median
description: The learner reports the median when the mean is asked, or vice versa.

title: Sum reported instead of mean
description: The learner adds the values but forgets to divide by the count.

title: Decimal given instead of percentage
description: The learner answers 0.3 when 30% is expected.

title: Percentage given instead of decimal
description: The learner answers 30 when 0.3 is expected.

title: Fraction reversed
description: Numerator and denominator swapped.

title: Mean treated as outlier-resistant
description: Believing the mean is unaffected by extreme values.

title: Chart axis misread
description: Reading the wrong axis or bar from a chart.

title: Correlation read as causation
description: Concluding that association proves cause.

title: Coordinate axes swapped
description: The learner plots (y, x) instead of (x, y) — the right pair of numbers, applied to the wrong axes.

title: Digits treated as numerical data
description: A variable written with digits (boat number, postcode) is classified as numerical even though its values are labels, not quantities.

title: The count changes between passes
description: The learner accepts two different totals for the same collection, treating a skipped or double-counted item as a property of the counting direction rather than an error.

title: The carried ten is dropped
description: When a column adds to more than nine the learner writes the units digit and forgets to carry the ten into the next column.

title: Digits subtracted in whichever order avoids borrowing
description: Within a column the learner takes the smaller digit from the larger one regardless of which is on top, instead of borrowing.

title: Multiplying treated as adding
description: The learner adds the two numbers instead of counting equal groups, so 7 x 4 is answered as 11.

title: Divided the wrong way round
description: The learner divides the number of groups by the amount being shared instead of the other way round.

title: Bigger bottom number read as a bigger fraction
description: The learner compares fractions by the size of the denominator alone, so 1/8 is judged larger than 1/4 because 8 is larger than 4.

title: More digits read as a bigger decimal
description: The learner compares decimals by how many digits follow the point, treating 0.25 as larger than 0.5 because it is longer.

title: A ratio part treated as a share of the whole
description: Given a ratio of 3 parts to 5 parts, the learner reports the first part as 3/5 of the mixture instead of 3/8.

title: Scaling by adding instead of multiplying
description: The learner keeps a difference constant rather than a ratio, so if 2 crates cost 6 coins they conclude 4 crates cost 8 coins.

title: Negatives ordered by their digits
description: The learner compares negative numbers by the digit after the minus sign, so -12 is judged larger than -7 because 12 is larger than 7.

title: Ticks counted instead of the scale being read
description: On a line whose labelled marks are more than one unit apart, the learner counts marks as if each were worth one, landing at a fraction of the intended value.

title: Right row, wrong column
description: The learner locates the correct case in a table but reads the value from a neighbouring column, answering a different variable's value.

title: A constant column counted as a variable
description: A column holding the same value on every row is treated as a variable simply because it has a header.

title: Cases and observations confused
description: Asked how many cases a dataset holds, the learner answers the number of recorded values — rows times columns — instead of the number of rows.
